title: A cleared cache does not cancel a read
takeaway: The caller retains the old promise. Generation and promise identity checks protect the new cache state.
assumptions: The first read starts a load and captures epoch E. The load succeeds. The optional second read uses the same pending key and starts before the old load completes. Vertical spacing shows order, not elapsed time. All participants are current-code context.

entities.label: Caller
entities.summary: Keeps the promise returned by read(). Other callers can share that promise.

entities.label: Revision cache
entities.summary: Owns epoch, saved, pending, priorities, and bytes.

entities.label: Asynchronous loader
entities.summary: The supplied load function returns a promise. clear() does not cancel it.

relationships.label: Read and retain P1
relationships.summary: read() registers the promise in pending and returns it to the caller.

relationships.label: Start load
relationships.summary: read() captures epoch before it calls load().

relationships.label: Clear owned state
relationships.summary: clear() advances epoch and clears the stores without cancelling the load.

relationships.label: Optional new read
relationships.summary: After pending is cleared, a new read can register a distinct promise for the same key.

relationships.label: Old load completes
relationships.summary: The old generation does not match epoch, so this completion cannot save its value.

relationships.label: Deliver through P1
relationships.summary: The completion returns value even when the generation check blocks storage.

relationships.label: Check promise identity
relationships.summary: finally() removes an entry only if it still holds this completion's promise.

plan.question: Who receives the old result, and why can it not change cache state after clear()?
plan.visualApproach: Use three fixed participant lanes and ordered messages. Put clear(), the generation comparison, and pending ownership inside the cache lane.
plan.whyThisForm: The sequence separates the caller's retained promise from the cache's removable reference. Vertical order shows how a newer promise can exist before the old cleanup.
plan.encodings: Columns show responsibility. Rows show operation order. Solid arrows show calls or result delivery. The cache boundary contains its state changes. P1 and P2 identify distinct promises.
plan.motion: Use a static sequence. The ordered rows keep the retained promise, clear operation, and later completion visible together; motion adds no necessary information.
plan.prediction: Without the optional second read, the old caller still receives the value, saved stays empty, and finally() finds no pending entry to delete.
plan.restingState: The full sequence shows P1 retained by the caller, the epoch mismatch, and P2 retained in pending.

scenarios.title: Old completion after clear()
scenarios.input: A pending read is cleared; an optional new read starts for the same key before the old load completes.

frames.title: Result delivery and cache ownership are separate
frames.caption: Read from top to bottom. The optional new read creates P2; the old completion still delivers through P1.
